title: Shadow-eval automation for embedding + reranker on config/model changes
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Summary: Implement an automated 'shadow-eval' pipeline that runs offline embedding + reranker quality checks whenever a model binary or serving configuration (quantization profile, batching policy, KV cache policy, route mapping) changes. The goal is to surface statistically significant regressions in recall/precision and detect distributional drift before changes reach production traffic. This ticket covers data sampling, eval orchestration, statistical tests, alerting thresholds, integration with CI/CD and the Console, and a minimal rollout plan.

Motivation: We have frequent model and config updates (quantization variants, new kernel selections, routing fallbacks). Human-led eval runs are slow and inconsistent. A low-friction automated shadow run will catch regressions early, reduce manual review load, and enable deterministic gating for sensitive customers and dedicated instances.

Out-of-scope: Online A/B experimentation, live traffic labeling, or full retraining pipelines. This ticket focuses on offline evals using curated prompt/reference sets + production-sampled probe queries and deterministic metrics (recall@k, MRR, nDCG, precision@k), plus drift statistics (feature distribution KL, embedding cosine similarity drift).
acceptance_criteria: Shadow-eval pipeline triggers automatically for: model version changes, quantization/profile flips, and runtime config updates (batch size, KV cache policy, kernel_override).

Each run executes a standard suite: curated eval set (gold), sampled probe set (recent production queries), and synthetic stress tests; outputs per-metric delta against baseline and p-values for statistical significance.

Alerting rules are created: high-confidence regression (p<0.01 and relative drop > 3% on recall@10) creates a blocking incident in PagerDuty during business hours; medium regressions create a Slack alert to #platform-evals.
Results are written to the Eval DB and surfaced in Console: per-route breakdown, top failing prompts, and suggested mitigations (rollback to last-good model or switch to float16 profile).
CI integration: PRs that change serving config include a link to the latest shadow-eval result; failing 'regression sentinel' prevents merge for protected branches.
Run cost is bounded: daily runs for mainline branches and on-demand runs for ad-hoc config flips. The system includes throttles to keep GPU spend under the project budget spreadsheet estimates.
tasks: Design sampling strategy: combine curated gold set (5k examples), rolling probe window (last 72 hours, stratified by route and doc length), and synthetic stress patterns.
Implement scaffold job in CI to schedule shadow-eval after model/config change; use ephemeral Dedicated pools or low-priority instances for evaluation.
Build eval harness (Python) that computes recall@k, MRR, nDCG, pairwise significance tests (bootstrap + t-test), and embedding drift stats (cosine mean shift, KL over binned norms).
Create datastore schema for eval runs and diffs; include links to binaries, config versions, and artifact hashes.
Integrate with Console: new view for shadow-eval runs, failure triage UI, and quick rollback button linking to Deployment manager.
Define alerting rules and PagerDuty escalation; add Slack summaries with top 10 failing prompts and metric deltas.
Add CI gate: fail protected-branch merges if a blocking regression is detected for that branch's target serving config.
Write runbook and playbook for oncall to triage shadow-eval regressions (diagnostics checklist, quick mitigations, stakeholder notification templates).

2026-03-11 — Rafael Gomez: Proposed sampling mix updated; recommend 70% probe sample, 20% gold set, 10% synthetic stress. See design doc section 3.1.
2026-03-11 — Lydia Chen (ML Infra): Suggest using bootstrap confidence intervals instead of only t-tests due to heavy-tailed retrieval scores. Will add a small library we already use for LLM evals.
2026-03-12 — Product (Markus Vogel): Request an explicit flag to opt dedicated customers into stricter gating; we should include customer opt-in metadata on runs.

notes: Privacy: probe samples must be stripped of PII per privacy playbook; PII filter implemented in upstream sampler (ENG-23611). Ensure KMS keys are used for storing any artifact snapshots.
implementation_risks: False positives from small sample sizes — mitigated by bootstrap CI and minimum sample thresholds per route.
GPU cost explosion if eval runs are left unconstrained — mitigated via throttles and low-priority nodes.
Alert fatigue — mitigate with two-tier alerting and human-in-the-loop confirmation for blocking rollbacks.
